The activity will integrate mechanistic models of tumour growth and invasion with experimental data obtained from in vitro multicellular systems. Particular attention will be devoted to tumour–microenvironment interactions, including active wetting, tissue remodelling, adhesion, friction, traction and cell migration. Single ventricle defects are among the most severe forms of congenital heart disease and are palliated through a series of surgeries culminating in the Fontan procedure. Although patient survival is substantially improved, progressive circulatory failure may develop over time, requiring heart support. However, current ventricular assist devices are poorly suited to the unique physiology of the Fontan circulation. Field: Physics / 02/PHYS-03 Fisica sperimentale della materia e applicazioni

The research activities are in the framework of the MIDSENSE project. MIDSENSE aims to develop and experimentally validate a fully integrated mid-infrared (MIR) sensing platform based entirely on silicon-compatible photonics technologies. The core objective is the realization of Ge/SiGe Quantum Cascade Detectors (QCDs)[1,2] monolithically integrated within silicon photonic circuits to enable compact, scalable, and low-noise molecular sensing systems operating in the MIR fingerprint region.
